metadata.title: Refined Absorption: A New Proof of the Existence Conjecture

nodes.name: Steiner System / Design
nodes.statement: A \emph{Steiner system} with parameters $(n,q,r)$ is a set $S$ of $q$-subsets of an $n$-set $X$ such that every $r$-subset of $X$ belongs to exactly one element of $S$; a \emph{design} with parameters $(n,q,r,\lambda)$ allows each $r$-subset to belong to exactly $\lambda$ elements of $S$.

nodes.name: Existence Conjecture
nodes.statement: Let $q > r \ge 2$ and $\lambda \geq 1$ be integers. If $n$ is sufficiently large and $\binom{q-i}{r-i}~|~\lambda \binom{n-i}{r-i}$ for all $0\le i \le r-1$, then there exists a design with parameters $(n,q,r,\lambda)$.
conclusions: There exists a design with parameters $(n,q,r,\lambda)$

nodes.name: Existence Conjecture (Keevash)
nodes.statement: The Existence Conjecture is true.

nodes.name: Absorber
nodes.statement: Let $L$ be a $K_q^r$-divisible hypergraph. A hypergraph $A$ is a \emph{$K_q^r$-absorber} for $L$ if $V(L)\subseteq V(A)$ is independent in $A$ and both $A$ and $L\cup A$ admit $K_q^r$ decompositions.

nodes.name: Absorber Existence (GKLO)
nodes.statement: Let $q > r\ge 1$ be integers. If $L$ is a $K_q^r$-divisible hypergraph, then there exists a $K_q^r$-absorber for $L$.

nodes.name: Omni-Absorber
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a hypergraph. $A$ is a \emph{$K_q^r$-omni-absorber} for $X$ with decomposition family $\mathcal{H}$ and decomposition function $\mathcal{Q}_A$ if $V(X)=V(A)$, $X,A$ are edge-disjoint, $\mathcal{H}$ are $K_q^r$-isomorphic subgraphs of $X\cup A$ with $|H\cap X|\le 1$, and for every $K_q^r$-divisible $L\subseteq X$, $\mathcal{Q}_A(L)\subseteq \mathcal{H}$ are pairwise edge-disjoint with $\bigcup \mathcal{Q}_A(L)=L\cup A$.

nodes.name: Refined Omni-Absorber
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a family of subgraphs of a hypergraph $G$. For $e\in G$, $\mathcal{H}(e):=\{H\in \mathcal{H}: e\in H\}$. A $K_q^r$-omni-absorber $A$ for $X$ with decomposition family $\mathcal{H}$ is \emph{$C$-refined} if $|\mathcal{H}(e)|\le C$ for every edge $e\in X\cup A$.

nodes.name: Refined Omni-Absorber Theorem
nodes.statement: For all integers $q > r\ge 1$, there exist $C\ge 1$ and $\varepsilon\in (0,1)$ such that: if $G$ is $r$-uniform on $n$ vertices with $\delta(G)\ge (1-\varepsilon)n$, $X$ a spanning subhypergraph with $\Delta(X)\le n/C$, and $\Delta:=\max\{\Delta(X), n^{1-1/r}\log n\}$, then there exists a $C$-refined $K_q^r$-omni-absorber $A\subseteq G$ for $X$ with $\Delta(A)\le C\cdot \Delta$.

nodes.name: Refiner
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be an $r$-uniform hypergraph. $R$ is a \emph{$K_q^r$-refiner} of $X$ with refinement family $\mathcal{H}$ and refinement function $\mathcal{Q}_R$ if $V(X)=V(R)$, $X,R$ edge-disjoint, $\mathcal{H}$ are $K_q^r$-divisible subgraphs of $X\cup R$ with $|H\cap X|\le 1$, and for every $K_q^r$-divisible $L\subseteq X$, $\mathcal{Q}_R(L)\subseteq \mathcal{H}$ pairwise edge-disjoint with $\bigcup \mathcal{Q}_R(L)=L\cup R$.

nodes.name: $C$-Refined Family
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{H}$ is \emph{$C$-refined} if $|\mathcal{H}(e)|\le C$ for every edge $e\in G$ and $\max\{v(H),e(H)\}\le C$ for every $H\in \mathcal{H}$.

nodes.name: $C$-Refined Refiner
nodes.statement: A $K_q^r$-refiner $R$ with refinement family $\mathcal{H}$ is \emph{$C$-refined} if $\mathcal{H}$ is $C$-refined. The \emph{refinement degree} $\Delta_{\mathcal{H}}(S)=|\{H\in\mathcal{H}:S\subseteq V(H)\}|$ for $S\in \binom{V(R)}{r-1}$, and $\Delta(\mathcal{H})=\max_S \Delta_{\mathcal{H}}(S)$.

nodes.name: Refiner Theorem
nodes.statement: For all integers $q>r\ge 1$, exist $C\ge 1$ and $\varepsilon\in (0,1)$ such that: if $G$ is $r$-uniform on $n$ vertices with $\delta(G)\ge (1-\varepsilon)n$, $X\subseteq G$ spanning with $\Delta(X)\le n/C$, $\Delta:=\max\{\Delta(X),n^{1-1/r}\log n\}$, then exists $C$-refined $K_q^r$-refiner $R\subseteq G$ of $X$ with refinement family $\mathcal{H}$ such that $\Delta(\mathcal{H})\le C\cdot \Delta$.

nodes.name: Design Hypergraph
nodes.statement: Let $F$ be a hypergraph. The \emph{$F$-design hypergraph of $G$}, ${\rm Design}_F(G)$, is the hypergraph $\mathcal{D}$ with $V(\mathcal{D})=E(G)$ and $E(\mathcal{D})=\{S\subseteq E(G): S\text{ isomorphic to } F\}$.

nodes.name: Random Reserve Lemma
nodes.statement: For all $q>r\ge 1$ integers, exists $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$: if $G$ is $r$-uniform with $\delta(G)\ge (1-\varepsilon)v(G)$ and $v(G)^{-\varepsilon}\le p\le 1$ and $v(G)\ge 1/\varepsilon$, then exists spanning $X\subseteq G$ with $\Delta(X)\le 2p\cdot v(G)$ and for all $e\in G\setminus X$, $\ge \varepsilon\cdot p^{\binom{q}{r}-1}\cdot v(G)^{q-r}$ $K_q^r$'s in $X\cup\{e\}$ contain $e$.
conclusions: For each $e\in G\setminus X$, at least $\varepsilon\cdot p^{\binom{q}{r}-1}\cdot v(G)^{q-r}$ $K_q^r$'s in $X\cup\{e\}$ contain $e$

nodes.name: Boost Lemma (special case)
nodes.statement: For all integers $q> r \ge 1$, exists $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$ and $C\ge 1$: if $J$ is $K_q^r$-divisible $r$-uniform with $v(J)\ge C$ and $\delta(J) \ge (1-\varepsilon)v(J)$, then exists subhypergraph $H$ of ${\rm Design}_{K_q^r}(J)$ with $d_H(v) = (1 \pm v(J)^{-(q-r)/3}) \cdot \frac{1}{2(q-r)!} \cdot v(J)^{q-r}$ for all $v\in V(H)$.
conclusions: Exists subhypergraph $H$ of ${\rm Design}_{K_q^r}(J)$ with near-regular degree as stated

nodes.name: RMH Construction
nodes.statement: Let $q\ge 1$. If $X$ is a set of vertices, exists $q$-uniform hypergraph $H$ and $X'\subseteq R:=V(H)\setminus X$ such that: (1) $X\subseteq V(H)$ and $|e\cap X|\le 1$ for all $e\in E(H)$; (2) $v(H)=(q+1)v(X)$; (3) $\Delta(H)\le 2q$ and $e(H)\le 2(q+1)v(X)$; (4) $|X'|=q-1$ and for every $L\subseteq X$ exists matching $M_L$ with $(L\cup R)\setminus X'\subseteq V(M_L)\subseteq L\cup R$.
conclusions: Exists $q$-uniform hypergraph $H$ and $X'\subseteq R:=V(H)\setminus X$ with properties (1)-(4)

nodes.name: Proof of RMH Construction
nodes.statement: Construct edges of $H$ from explicit enumeration $y_1,\ldots, y_{(q+1)m}$ where $y_{(q+1)i}=x_i$. Define edges as size-$q$ consecutive intervals (and an alternate version skipping multiples of $q+1$). Verify (1)-(4) by computing $\Delta(H)$, $v(H)$ and constructing the explicit matching $M_L$.

nodes.name: Refiner/Omni-Absorber for $r=1$
nodes.statement: Theorem~\ref{thm:Omni} and Theorem~\ref{thm:Refiner} hold for $r=1$ with $C=2q$.
conclusions: $C=2q$ suffices in Theorems Refined Omni-Absorber and Refiner

nodes.name: $A$-perfect matching
nodes.statement: A matching of $G$ is \emph{$A$-perfect} if every vertex of $A$ is in an edge of the matching.

nodes.name: Bipartite Hypergraph
nodes.statement: A hypergraph $G=(A,B)$ is \emph{bipartite with parts $A$ and $B$} if $V(G)=A\cup B$ and every edge contains exactly one vertex from $A$.

nodes.name: Nibble with Reserves
nodes.statement: For each $r\ge 2$, $\beta\in (0,1)$, exist $D_\beta\ge 0$, $\alpha\in (0,1)$: for $D\ge D_\beta$, if $G=G_1\cup G_2$ ($r$-uniform multi-hypergraph) with codegrees $\le D^{1-\beta}$, where $G_2=(A,B)$ is bipartite, $\deg_{G_2}(B)\le D$, $\deg_{G_2}(A)\ge D^{1-\alpha}$, $\deg_{G_1}(\cdot)\le D$, $\deg_{G_1}(A)\ge D(1-D^{-\beta})$, then exists $A$-perfect matching of $G$.
assumptions: $G=G_1\cup G_2$ edge-disjoint with bipartite $G_2=(A,B)$ as stated
Stated minimum/maximum degree conditions on $G_1, G_2$

nodes.name: Multi-Omni-Absorber
nodes.statement: A multi-hypergraph $A$ is a \emph{$K_q^r$-multi-omni-absorber} if it satisfies the definition of $K_q^r$-omni-absorber except that $X\cup A$ may not be simple.

nodes.name: Multi-Refiner
nodes.statement: A multi-hypergraph $R$ is a \emph{$K_q^r$-multi-refiner} of $X$ if it satisfies the definition of $K_q^r$-refiner except that $X\cup R$ may not be simple.

nodes.name: $M(q,r)$
nodes.statement: For all integers $q>r\ge 1$, $M(q,r):={\rm lcm}\left(\binom{q-i}{r-i}: i\in\{0,1,\ldots,r-1\}\right)$.

nodes.name: $i$-flat to $Y$
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a hypergraph and $Y\subseteq V(X)$. For nonnegative $i$, $X$ is \emph{$i$-flat to $Y$} if $|e\setminus Y|\le i$ for all $e\in E(X)$.

nodes.name: Refined Multi-Omni-Absorber Theorem
nodes.statement: For all $q>r\ge 1$ integers, exists $C\ge 1$: if $X$ is $r$-uniform multi-hypergraph of multiplicity $\le M(q,r)$ with $v(X)\ge C$, $\Delta:=\max\{\Delta(X),v(X)^{1-1/r}\log v(X)\}$, $Y\subseteq V(X)$ with $|Y|\ge v(X)/3$, then exists $C$-refined $K_q^r$-multi-omni-absorber $A$ for $X$ with (1) $\Delta(A)\le C\cdot \Delta$ and (2) $A$ is $(r-1)$-flat to $Y$.

nodes.name: Multi-Refiner Theorem
nodes.statement: For all $q>r\ge 1$, exists $C\ge 1$: assuming Theorem~\ref{thm:MultiOmni} for all $r'\in [r-1]$, if $X$ is $r$-uniform multi-hypergraph with multiplicity $\le M(q,r)$ and $v(X)\ge C$, $\Delta:=\max\{\Delta(X),v(X)^{1-1/r}\log v(X)\}$, $|Y|\ge v(X)/3$, then exists $C$-refined $K_q^r$-multi-refiner $R$ of $X$ with $\Delta(\mathcal{H})\le C\Delta$ and $R$ is $(r-1)$-flat to $Y$.

nodes.name: Multi-Refiner with Remainder
nodes.statement: $R$ is a \emph{$K_q^r$-multi-refiner} of $X$ with \emph{remainder} $X'\subseteq X\cup R$, refinement family $\mathcal{H}$, function $\mathcal{Q}_R$ if $X,R$ edge-disjoint, $R$ is $K_q^r$-divisible, $\mathcal{H}$ is $K_q^r$-divisible subgraphs with $|H\cap X|\le 1$ and $H\cap X\cap X'=\emptyset$, and for every $K_q^r$-divisible $L\subseteq X$, $\mathcal{Q}_R(L)\subseteq \mathcal{H}$ with $(L\cup R)\setminus X'\subseteq \bigcup \mathcal{Q}_R(L)\subseteq L\cup R$. The \emph{$L$-leftover} is $L':=(L\cup R)\setminus \bigcup \mathcal{Q}_R(L)$.

nodes.name: Concatenating Refiners
nodes.statement: If $R_i$ is a $C_i$-refined $K_q^r$-multi-refiner of $X_i$ with remainder $X_{i+1}$ for $i\in \{1,2\}$, and $R_1,R_2$ are edge-disjoint, then $R:=R_1\cup R_2$ is a $(C_1+C_2)$-refined $K_q^r$-multi-refiner of $X_1$ with remainder $X_3$, family $\mathcal{H}_1\cup \mathcal{H}_2$, and $\Delta(\mathcal{H})\le \Delta(\mathcal{H}_1)+\Delta(\mathcal{H}_2)$.
conclusions: $R_1\cup R_2$ is $(C_1+C_2)$-refined multi-refiner of $X_1$ with remainder $X_3$

nodes.name: Proof of Concatenating Refiners
nodes.statement: Establish $K_q^r$-divisibility of $R$, verify intersection conditions on $X_1, X_2, X_3$, then for $K_q^r$-divisible $L\subseteq X_1$ track $L_1=(L\cup R_1)\setminus \bigcup \mathcal{Q}_{R_1}(L)$ through both refiners.

nodes.name: Edge Sparsification Lemma
nodes.statement: For all $q>r\ge 2$, exists $C\ge 1$: if $X$ is $r$-uniform multi-hypergraph with multiplicity $\le M(q,r)$, $v(X)\ge C$, $\Delta(X)\ge v(X)^{1-1/r}\log v(X)$, $|Y|\ge v(X)/3$, then exists $C$-refined $K_q^r$-multi-refiner $R$ of $X$ with remainder $X'\subseteq R$ and (1) $\Delta(\mathcal{H})\le C\Delta(X)$, (2) $R$ is $(r-1)$-flat to $Y$, (3) $\Delta(X')\le v(X)^{1-1/r}$, (4) $X'$ has multiplicity $\le M(q,r)$.

nodes.name: Refine Down Lemma
nodes.statement: For all $q>r\ge 2$, exists $C\ge 1$: assuming MultiOmni for $r'\in [r-1]$, if $X$ has multiplicity $\le M(q,r)$, $\Delta:=\max\{\Delta(X),v(X)^{1-1/r}\log v(X)\}$, $|Y|\ge C$, then exists $C$-refined $K_q^r$-multi-refiner $R$ of $X$ with remainder $X'$ such that (1) $\Delta(\mathcal{H})\le C\cdot (v(X)/|Y|)^{\binom{r}{2}}\cdot \Delta$, (2) $R$ is $(r-1)$-flat to $Y$, (3) $\Delta(X')$ bounded similarly, (4) $X'$ has multiplicity $\le M(q,r)$ and $V(X')\subseteq Y$.
conclusions: Conditions (1)-(4) on bounds and flatness as stated

nodes.name: Better Refine Down Lemma
nodes.statement: For all $q>r\ge 2$, exists $C\ge 1$: assuming MultiOmni for $r'\in [r-1]$, if $X$ has multiplicity $\le M(q,r)$, $v(X)\ge C$, $\Delta:=\max\{\Delta(X),C\cdot v(X)^{1-1/r}\log v(X)\}$, $|Y|\ge v(X)/3$, then exists $C$-refined $K_q^r$-multi-refiner $R$ of $X$ with remainder $X'$ satisfying (1) $\Delta(\mathcal{H})\le C\Delta$, (2) $R$ is $(r-1)$-flat to $Y$, (3) $\Delta(X')\le \Delta/2$, (4) $X'$ multiplicity $\le M(q,r)$ and $V(X')\subseteq Y$.
conclusions: $\Delta(\mathcal{H})\le C\Delta$, $R$ is $(r-1)$-flat to $Y$, $\Delta(X')\le \Delta/2$, $X'$ multiplicity $\le M(q,r)$ and $V(X')\subseteq Y$

nodes.name: Proof of Better Refine Down Lemma
nodes.statement: Apply Edge Sparsification Lemma followed by Refine Down Lemma; concatenate via Proposition~\ref{prop:Concatenate}, balancing constants so the decrease from sparsification offsets the increase from refine-down.

nodes.name: Case: $\Delta(X) < \Delta_1$
nodes.statement: Apply the Refine Down Lemma directly to $X$ and $Y$; bounds follow because $\Delta\ge 2C_2\cdot 3^{\binom{r}{2}}\cdot \Delta_1$ when $C$ is large.

nodes.name: Case: $\Delta_1 = \Delta(X)$
nodes.statement: Apply Edge Sparsification Lemma to obtain $R_1$ with remainder $X_2$, then apply Refine Down Lemma to $X_2$ to get $R_2$. Take $R = R_1\cup R_2$.

nodes.name: Concatenate and verify bounds
nodes.statement: By Proposition~\ref{prop:Concatenate}, $R$ is multi-refiner; verify $\Delta(\mathcal{H}_1)+\Delta(\mathcal{H}_2)\le C\Delta$ and $\Delta(X_3)\le \Delta/2$.

nodes.name: Proof of Multi-Refiner Theorem
nodes.statement: Iterate the Better Refine Down Lemma until the remainder has constant size, with a strengthened inductive statement that includes a per-edge refinement bound. Induction on $v(X)$.

nodes.name: Setup constants and inductive statement
nodes.statement: Define $C_0$ depending on $C',M(q,r),r$, set up stronger inductive claim with conditions (1)-(3) including per-edge refinement bound $\le C_0/2$.

nodes.name: Apply Better Refine Down to get $R_1$
nodes.statement: Choose $Y'\subseteq Y$ with $|Y'|=\lceil v(X)/3\rceil$. By Lemma BetterRefineDown, get $C'$-refined refiner $R_1$ with remainder $X'$ satisfying (1)-(4).

nodes.name: Construct $R_2$ via induction or direct construction
nodes.statement: If $v(X')\ge C'$, apply induction to $X', Y'$. Otherwise, build $R_2$ by direct multiplicity-$M(q,r)$ scaling and explicit refinement family covering all $K_q^r$-divisible subgraphs of $X'$.

nodes.name: Combine $R=R_1\cup R_2$ and verify (1)-(3)
nodes.statement: Use Proposition Concatenate. Verify bounds for $\Delta(\mathcal{H})$, flatness, and per-edge refinement counts in cases $e\in X\setminus X'$, $X\cap X'$, $R_1$, $R_2$.

nodes.name: Multiplicity Reduction Lemma
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be $r$-uniform multi-hypergraph; $R$ has $|R(S)|=M(q,r)|X(S)|$, $X'\subseteq R$ has $|X'(S)|=M(q,r)-1$ where $|R(S)|\ne 0$. Then $R$ is a $2M(q,r)$-refined $K_q^r$-multi-refiner of $X$ with remainder $X'$, family $\mathcal{H}$, $\Delta(\mathcal{H})\le 2M(q,r)\Delta(X)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Multiplicity Reduction Lemma
nodes.statement: For each $r$-set $S$ with $|X(S)|\ne 0$, apply Proposition RMHG to $X_S, R_S, X'_S$ to get $H_S$. Build $\mathcal{H}_S$ as the corresponding $S$-attached subgraphs. For $K_q^r$-divisible $L\subseteq X$, use the matchings $M_{S,L}$ from RMHG part (4) to assemble $\mathcal{H}_L$.

nodes.name: Quasi-Random Partition
nodes.statement: If $k$ is a positive integer with $\Delta(X)\ge 3k(\log(2k)+(r-1)\log v(X))$, then exists partition $V_1,\ldots,V_k$ of $V(X)$ with $|V_i|\le 2v(X)/k$ and for every $(r-1)$-subset $S$, $|X(S)\cap V_i|\le 2\Delta(X)/k$ for all $i$.

nodes.name: Proof of Quasi-Random Partition
nodes.statement: Place each vertex into a part uniformly at random. Bound the bad events $A_i$ (size violation) and $A_{S,i}$ (codegree violation) via Chernoff; union bound completes.

nodes.name: Non-Uniform Turan
nodes.statement: Let $Z$ be a $q$-bounded hypergraph with at least $q$ vertices. For each $i\in [q]$, $\alpha_i:=|\{e\in Z:|e|=i\}|/\binom{v(Z)}{i}$, $\alpha:=\sum \alpha_i\binom{q}{i}$. Then number of $q$-subsets of $V(Z)$ spanning an edge of $Z$ is $\le \alpha\binom{v(Z)}{q}$; if $\alpha<1$ exists $q$-subset spanning none.
conclusions: Number of $q$-subsets of $V(Z)$ spanning an edge $\le \alpha\binom{v(Z)}{q}$
If $\alpha<1$, exists $q$-subset of $V(Z)$ spanning no edge

nodes.name: Proof of Non-Uniform Turan
nodes.statement: For each $i$, $|A_i|\le |\{e\in Z:|e|=i\}|\binom{v(Z)-i}{q-i}=\alpha_i\binom{q}{i}\binom{v(Z)}{q}$; sum over $i$ gives bound.

nodes.name: Special Sets Lemma
nodes.statement: For all $q>r\ge 1$, exists $C\ge 1$: if $v(X)\ge C$, $24r\le k\le v(X)^{(r-1)/r}/C$, $\mathcal{I}$ is $r$-multi-subsets of $[k]$, $V_1,\ldots,V_k$ a quasi-random partition, $|Y|\ge v(X)/3$, then exists $\mathcal{S}=(S_I:I\in \mathcal{I})$ with (1) $|S_I|=q-r$, $S_I\subseteq Y\setminus \bigcup_{i\in I}V_i$; (2) $|S_{I_1}\cap S_{I_2}|\le r-2$ for $I_1\ne I_2$; (3) bounded co-occurrence $|\{S_I:T\subseteq S_I, J\subseteq I\}|\le \lceil C k^{|T|+1}/v(X)^{|T|}\rceil$.

nodes.name: Proof of Special Sets Lemma
nodes.statement: Greedy maximal extension: choose maximal $\mathcal{I}'\subseteq \mathcal{I}$, $\mathcal{S}'$ satisfying (1)-(3). For $I\not\in\mathcal{I}'$, build bad sets $B_\ell$ and apply Proposition NonUniformTuran to find a valid $S_I$, contradicting maximality.

nodes.name: Proof of Edge Sparsification Lemma
nodes.statement: Pick $k\approx v(X)^{(r-1)/r}$. Use Quasi-Random Partition then Special Sets Lemma to assign $S_I$ for each $I$. For each $e\in X$ embed $M(q,r)$ private cliques on $e\cup S_{\phi(e)}$. Reduce remainder multiplicity via Multiplicity Reduction Lemma. Verify (1)-(4).

nodes.name: Choose $k$ and partition
nodes.statement: Set $k:=\lfloor v(X)^{1-1/r}/(8q\cdot 2^r\cdot M(q,r)\cdot C')\rfloor$. Apply Proposition QuasiRandomPartition.

nodes.name: Apply Special Sets Lemma
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma SpecialSets to $X$ and $Y$ with the chosen $k$ and partition to obtain $\mathcal{S}$.

nodes.name: Build $R_1$ via private cliques
nodes.statement: For each edge $e\in X$, add $M(q,r)$ edge-disjoint copies $P_{i,e}$ of $\binom{e\cup S_{\phi(e)}}{r}\setminus e$. Define refinement family $\mathcal{H}_1=\{e\cup P_{1,e}:e\in X\}$.

nodes.name: Apply Multiplicity Reduction
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma MRL to obtain $R_2$ with remainder $X_3$. By Proposition Concatenate, $R=R_1\cup R_2$ is a $C$-refined multi-refiner.

nodes.name: Verify $\Delta(\mathcal{H})$ bound
nodes.statement: Compute $|R_1(S)|$ for $S\in \binom{V(X)}{r-1}$ summing over $T\subseteq S$. Show $\Delta(R_1)\le 4^r C' \sqrt{C}\Delta(X)$, hence $\Delta(\mathcal{H})\le C\Delta(X)$.

nodes.name: Verify flatness and remainder bounds
nodes.statement: Show $R_1$ (and hence $R$) is $(r-1)$-flat to $Y$ since each $P_{i,e}$ contains a vertex of $S_{\phi(e)}\subseteq Y$. Compute $|X_3(S)|\le v(X)^{1-1/r}$ via case split on $T\subseteq S$.

nodes.name: Refine Down Lemma - One Step
nodes.statement: For all $q>r\ge 2$, exists $C>1$: assuming MultiOmni for $r'\in [r-1]$, if $X$ has multiplicity $\le M(q,r)$, $\Delta:=\max\{\Delta(X),v(X)^{1-1/r}\log v(X)\}$, $|Y|\ge C$, $i\in [r]$ with $X$ $i$-flat to $Y$, $Z\supseteq Y$ with $|Z|\ge 2C|Y|$, then exists $C$-refined $K_q^r$-multi-refiner $R$ of $X$ with remainder $X'$ satisfying (1)-(6) including bounded refinement degree by $|T\setminus Y|$ and $X'$ is $(i-1)$-flat to $Z$.

nodes.name: Local Multi-Refiner with Remainder
nodes.statement: Let $S\subseteq V(X)$ with $|S|=i$ such that $S\subseteq e$ for all $e\in E(X)$. $R$ is a \emph{local $K_q^r$-multi-refiner} of $X$ at $S$ with remainder $X'\subseteq X\cup R$, family $\mathcal{H}$, if $X,R$ edge-disjoint, $R$ $K_q^r$-divisible, $\mathcal{H}$ are $K_q^r$-divisible subgraphs with $|H\cap X|\le 1$, and for every subgraph $L\subseteq X$ with $L(S)$ being $K_{q-i}^{r-i}$-divisible, exists edge-disjoint $H_1,\ldots,H_k\in \mathcal{H}$ with $(L\cup R)\setminus X'\subseteq \bigcup H_i\subseteq L\cup R$.

nodes.name: Link Divisibility
nodes.statement: If $L$ is $K_q^r$-divisible $r$-uniform (multi)-hypergraph, $i\in[r-1]$, $S\in \binom{V(L)}{i}$, then $L(S)$ is $K_{q-i}^{r-i}$-divisible.

nodes.name: Proof of Link Divisibility
nodes.statement: For $j\in [r-1-i]$ and $T\in \binom{V(L)\setminus S}{j}$, $\binom{q-(i+j)}{r-(i+j)}\mid d_L(S\cup T)=d_{L(S)}(T)$.

nodes.name: Local Multi-Refiner Theorem
nodes.statement: For all $q>r\ge 2$, exists $C>1$: for $i\in[r-1]$, assuming MRT holds for $r':=r-i$, if $X$ has multiplicity $\le M(q,r)$, $\Delta:=\max\{\Delta(X),v(X)^{1-1/r}\log v(X)\}$, exists $S\subseteq V(X)$ with $|S|=i$ and $S\subseteq e$ for all $e$, exists $Y\subseteq V(X)$ with $|Y|\le v(X)/C$ and $e\subseteq Y$ for all $e\in X$, then exists $C$-refined local $K_q^r$-multi-refiner $R$ at $S$ satisfying (1)-(5).
assumptions: $Y\subseteq V(X)$, $|Y|\le v(X)/C$, $e\subseteq Y$ for all $e\in X$

nodes.name: Proof of Local Multi-Refiner Theorem
nodes.statement: Apply MultiOmni inductively for $r-i$ to $X(S)$ to get $A$. For each $K_{q-i}^{r-i}$ subgraph $H\in \mathcal{H}'$, augment $H$ with edges to make $H\cup S$ a $K_q^r$, controlling multiplicities. Verify refinement, divisibility, flatness.

nodes.name: Apply MultiOmni to $X(S)$
nodes.statement: By induction (MultiOmni for $r-i$), get $C'$-refined $K_{q-i}^{r-i}$-multi-omni-absorber $A$ of $X(S)$ with $\Delta(A)\le C'\Delta$ and $A$ is $(r-1-i)$-flat to $V(X)\setminus(S\cup Y)$.

nodes.name: Add $K_q^r$-divisibility edges
nodes.statement: For each $H\in \mathcal{Q}$ and $T\in \binom{V(H)\cup S}{r}$ with $S\setminus T\ne \emptyset$, add $M(q,r)+1$ edges; for $H\in \mathcal{H}'\setminus \mathcal{Q}$, add $M(q,r)$ edges. Define $\phi(H)$ extending $H$.

nodes.name: Verify $C$-refined and decomposition properties
nodes.statement: Each $H\in \mathcal{H}$ is $K_q^r$, $|\mathcal{H}(e)|\le C'$ for $e\in X$ and $\le 1$ for $e\in R$. For $L\subseteq X$ with $K_{q-i}^{r-i}$-divisible $L(S)$, $\mathcal{H}'_L$ decomposes $L\cup A$.

nodes.name: Verify bounds (1)-(5)
nodes.statement: Bound $\Delta_\mathcal{H}(T)$ for $S\subseteq T$ via $C'\cdot M(q,r)\Delta$. For $S\setminus T\ne \emptyset$, $\Delta_\mathcal{H}(T)\le \binom{r-1}{r-i}C'\le C$. Verify flatness and $\Delta(X')\le C$.

nodes.name: Proof of One-Step Refine Down Lemma
nodes.statement: For each $i$-set $S$ in $X\setminus Z$, apply Theorem MLRT to $X_S=S\uplus X(S)$ to get local multi-refiner $R_S$. Randomly permute the embedding of $R_S$ on $Z\setminus Y$. Use Chernoff and union bound to show desired bounds hold for some choice of permutations.

nodes.name: Apply MLRT to each $i$-set $S$
nodes.statement: For each $S\in \binom{X\setminus Z}{i}$, by MLRT exists $C'$-refined local $K_q^r$-multi-refiner $R_S$ of $X_S$ at $S$ with refinement family $\mathcal{H}_S$ satisfying (1)-(5).

nodes.name: Random permutation of $Z\setminus Y$
nodes.statement: For each $i$-set $S$, choose random permutation $\sigma_S$ of $Z\setminus Y$; let $R:=\bigcup_S R_{S,\sigma_S}$, $\mathcal{H}:=\bigcup_S \mathcal{H}_{S,\sigma_S}$.

nodes.name: Verify (1), (3), (4) deterministically
nodes.statement: For $|T\setminus Y|=i$, $\Delta_\mathcal{H}(T)=\Delta_{\mathcal{H}_{S,\sigma_S}}(T)\le C'\Delta\le C\Delta$ giving (1). Construction yields (3) and (4) for all permutations.

nodes.name: Bound $\Expect{|Z_T|}$ (Claim)
nodes.statement: Show $\Expect{|Z_T|}\le \mu := (C')^{r-1}\max\{(v(X)/|Y|)^{i-1}\Delta, (v(X)/|Y|)^{\min\{i,r-1\}}\}$ via two cases on $|T\cap Y|$.

nodes.name: Chernoff + union bound for (2), (5)
nodes.statement: Apply Chernoff: $\Prob{|Z_T|>2\mu}<1/(2v(X)^{r-1})$. Union bound over $T$ gives positive probability that no $A_T$ or $B_T$ occurs, yielding desired permutations.

nodes.name: Proof of Refine Down Lemma
nodes.statement: Choose nested subsets $Y_r\subseteq \ldots \subseteq Y_0\subseteq Y$. By extremal choice of refiner $R$ minimizing $i$ (failure level), and assuming $i>0$, apply One-Step Refine Down Lemma to $X', Y_i, Y_{i-1}$ to derive contradiction. Hence $i=0$.

nodes.name: Setup nested $Y_i$ and inductive structure
nodes.statement: Choose $Y_r\subseteq \ldots \subseteq Y_0\subseteq Y$ with $|Y_r|\ge C'$, $|Y_0|\ge |Y|/(2C')$, $|Y_i|=2C'|Y_{i+1}|$. Define conditions $(1)_i$-$(6)_i$.

nodes.name: Extremal choice of $R$ minimizing $i$
nodes.statement: Choose $R, \mathcal{H}, X'$ satisfying $(1)_i$-$(6)_i$ with $i$ minimized; if $i=0$, conclude. Otherwise derive contradiction.

nodes.name: Apply One-Step Refine Down to $X'$
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma RefineDownOneStep with parameters $X', Y_i, Y_{i-1}$ to get $R'$ with refinement family $\mathcal{H}'$ and remainder $X''$ satisfying $(1')$-$(6')$.

nodes.name: Concatenate $R\cup R'$ and verify $(1)_{i-1}$-$(6)_{i-1}$
nodes.statement: By Proposition Concatenate, $R'':=R\cup R'$ is $C_{i-1}$-refined. Verify all conditions; cases on $|T\setminus Y_i|$. Contradicts minimality of $i$.

nodes.name: Proof of Refined Multi-Omni-Absorber Theorem
nodes.statement: Apply MRT to get $C'$-refined multi-refiner $R$ with family $\mathcal{H}'$. Use Theorem AbsorberExistence to get absorber $A_H$ for each $H\in \mathcal{H}'$. Embed (Claim A) the $A_H'$ deterministically avoiding bad sets via Proposition NonUniformTuran. Define $A:=R\cup \bigcup A_H'$.

nodes.name: Apply MRT to $X, Y$
nodes.statement: By Theorem MRT, exists $C'$-refined $K_q^r$-multi-refiner $R$ of $X$ with refinement family $\mathcal{H}'$ such that $\Delta(\mathcal{H}')\le C'\Delta$ and $R$ is $(r-1)$-flat to $Y$.

nodes.name: Get private absorbers via Theorem AbsorberExistence
nodes.statement: By Theorem AbsorberExistence, for each $H\in \mathcal{H}'$ exists $K_q^r$-absorber $A_H$ with decompositions $\mathcal{Q}_{1,H}$ of $A_H$ and $\mathcal{Q}_{2,H}$ of $A_H\cup H$.

nodes.name: Embed absorbers via Claim A (avoid bad sets)
nodes.statement: Claim A: deterministically choose embeddings $A_H'\subseteq Y$ via maximal extension; bound $d_{A'}(J,U)\le m=C\Delta/(k\cdot 2^r)$ using Proposition NonUniformTuran on the bad sets $B_\ell$.

nodes.name: Verify $A$ is $C$-refined omni-absorber and (1)-(2)
nodes.statement: Define $\mathcal{H}=\bigcup \mathcal{Q}_{1,H}'\cup \mathcal{Q}_{2,H}'$. Verify $|\mathcal{H}(e)|\le C$, multi-omni-absorber property, $\Delta(A)\le C\Delta$, $(r-1)$-flatness.

nodes.name: Partial $K_k^r$ rooted at $S$
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be $r$-uniform. If $S\subseteq V(G)$ with $k>|S|\ge r$, a \emph{partial $K_k^r$ rooted at $S$} in $G$ is a subgraph $T$ with $S\subseteq V(T)$, $|T|=k$, $\binom{V(T)}{r}\setminus \binom{S}{r}\subseteq E(G)$.

nodes.name: Partial Clique Embedding Lemma
nodes.statement: For all $h\ge r\ge 1$, $k\ge 1$ exist $C\ge 1$, $\varepsilon,\gamma\in (0,1)$: if $G$ $r$-uniform with $v(G)\ge C$, $\delta(G)\ge (1-\varepsilon)v(G)$, $Y$ $h$-bounded multi-hypergraph with $V(Y)=V(G)$, $G,Y$ edge-disjoint, $\Delta_{r-1}(Y)\le \gamma v(G)$, $|e|\ge r$ for all $e\in E(Y)$, then exist edge-disjoint partial $K_{k+|e|}^r$'s $T_e$ rooted at $V(e)$ with $\Delta(T)\le C\Delta_{r-1}(Y)$ where $T:=\bigcup_e T_e$.

nodes.name: Proof of Partial Clique Embedding Lemma
nodes.statement: Greedy maximal extension of $Y'\subseteq Y$ and $\mathcal{T}'$. For $e\in Y\setminus Y'$, build avoidance sets $A_\ell$ (non-edges) and $B_\ell$ (overdense codegree) and apply Proposition NonUniformTuran to find $S$ avoiding both, contradicting maximality.

nodes.name: Anti-Edge / Fake Edge
nodes.statement: An \emph{anti-edge on $S$}, ${\rm AntiEdge}_q^r(S)$, is new vertices $x_1,\ldots,x_{q-r}$ with edges $\binom{S\cup\{x_i\}}{r}\setminus \{S\}$. A \emph{fake edge on $S$}, ${\rm FakeEdge}_q^r(S)$, is new vertices $x_1,\ldots,x_{q-r}$ with $\{{\rm AntiEdge}_q^r(T): T\in \binom{S\cup\{x_i\}}{r}\setminus\{S\}\}$.

nodes.name: Divisibility of Anti/Fake Edges
nodes.statement: (1) If $F={\rm AntiEdge}_q^r(S)$, then for $0\le i\le r-1$ and $S'\subseteq S$ with $|S'|=i$, $d_F(S')\equiv -1 \mod \binom{q-i}{r-i}$. (2) If $F={\rm FakeEdge}_q^r(S)$, $d_F(S')\equiv +1 \mod \binom{q-i}{r-i}$.

nodes.name: Edge-Disjoint Copies are Divisible
nodes.statement: (1) $M(q,r)$ edge-disjoint copies of ${\rm AntiEdge}_q^r(S)$ form a $K_q^r$-divisible hypergraph. (2) Same for $M(q,r)$ edge-disjoint copies of ${\rm FakeEdge}_q^r(S)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Refiner Theorem
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem MRT to get multi-refiner $R'$ with family $\mathcal{H}'$. Apply Lemma EmbedMinDegree with $Y:=R'$ to find edge-disjoint partial cliques $T_e\subseteq G\setminus E(X)$. Embed $U_e:={\rm FakeEdge}_q^r(V(e))$ inside $T_e$. Set $R:=\bigcup U_e$ and verify divisibility/refinement.

nodes.name: Apply MRT for multi-refiner
nodes.statement: By Theorem MRT, exists $C''$-refined $K_q^r$-multi-refiner $R'$ of $X$ with $\Delta(\mathcal{H}')\le C''\Delta'$, $R'$ is $(r-1)$-flat to $Y$.

nodes.name: Apply Partial Clique Embedding
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma EmbedMinDegree with $Y:=R'$, $h:=r$, $k:=q^{r+1}$ to get edge-disjoint partial $K_{k+|e|}^r$'s $T_e\subseteq G\setminus E(X)$ with $\Delta(T)\le C'\Delta(Y)$.

nodes.name: Embed fake edges
nodes.statement: For each $e\in E(Y)$, embed ${\rm FakeEdge}_q^r(V(e))$ inside $T_e$ as $U_e$. Define $R:=\bigcup_{e} U_e$ (simple $r$-uniform).

nodes.name: Verify divisibility and refinement
nodes.statement: By Fact Div, $\phi(H)$ is $K_q^r$-divisible for $H\in \mathcal{H}'$. Show $|\mathcal{H}(f)|\le C$ in cases $f\in R$ or $f\in X$. Conclude $R$ is $C$-refined $K_q^r$-refiner with $\Delta(\mathcal{H})\le C\Delta$.

nodes.name: Proof of Refined Omni-Absorber Theorem
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem Refiner to get $h$-refined $K_q^r$-refiner $R$. Use Theorem AbsorberExistence to get absorber $A_H$ for each $H\in \mathcal{H}'$. Apply Lemma EmbedMinDegree to embed partial cliques $T_e$, then absorbers $U_H$ inside. Set $A:=R\cup \bigcup U_H$ and verify it is $C$-refined omni-absorber with $\Delta(A)\le C\Delta$.

nodes.name: Apply Refiner Theorem
nodes.statement: By Theorem Refiner, exists $h$-refined $K_q^r$-refiner $R$ of $X$ with $\Delta(\mathcal{H})\le h\Delta'$.

nodes.name: Get absorbers and embed via Partial Clique
nodes.statement: Set $Y$ as $h$-bounded multi-hypergraph from refinement family. By Theorem AbsorberExistence get $A_H$. By Lemma EmbedMinDegree get partial cliques $T_e\subseteq G\setminus (X\cup R)$. Embed $A_H$ inside $T_H$ as $U_H$.

nodes.name: Verify $A$ is $C$-refined omni-absorber
nodes.statement: Define $A:=R\cup \bigcup U_H$, $\mathcal{H}:=\bigcup \mathcal{Q}_{1,H}\cup \mathcal{Q}_{2,H}$. Show $|\mathcal{H}(e)|\le C$. For $K_q^r$-divisible $L\subseteq X$, build $\mathcal{Q}_L$ decomposing $L\cup A$.

nodes.name: Bound $\Delta(A)\le C\Delta$
nodes.statement: $\Delta(A)\le \Delta(R)+\Delta(T)\le h^2\Delta'+C'\Delta_{r-1}(Y)\le h(h+C')\Delta'\le C\Delta$.

nodes.name: Proof of Random Reserve Lemma
nodes.statement: Choose $X$ by including each edge of $G$ independently with probability $p$. Bound bad events $A_S$ (degree exceeds $2pv(G)$) and $B_T$ (insufficient $K_q^r$ extensions) via Chernoff; union bound completes.

nodes.name: Existence Conjecture - Minimum Degree Version
nodes.statement: For all integers $q>r\ge 2$, exist $n_0$ and $\varepsilon>0$: for all $K_q^r$-divisible $r$-uniform hypergraphs $G$ with $v(G)\ge n_0$ and $\delta(G)\ge (1-\varepsilon)v(G)$, exists $K_q^r$-decomposition of $G$.

nodes.name: Proof of Existence Conjecture (Minimum Degree)
nodes.statement: Step 1: Apply Lemma RandomX to reserve $X\subseteq G$. Step 2: Apply Theorem Omni to get refined omni-absorber $A$. Step 3: Apply Lemma RegBoost to $J:=G\setminus (X\cup A)$. Step 4: Apply Theorem NibbleReserves to get $V(G_1)$-perfect matching $\mathcal{Q}_1$. Step 5: Use omni-absorber definition on leftover $L:=X\setminus Q_1$ to complete decomposition.

nodes.name: Reserve random $X$
nodes.statement: By Lemma RandomX, exists spanning $X\subseteq G$ with $\Delta(X)\le 2pv(G)=\Delta$ and many $K_q^r$ extensions for each edge.

nodes.name: Construct refined omni-absorber $A$
nodes.statement: By Theorem Omni, exists $C$-refined $K_q^r$-omni-absorber $A\subseteq G$ for $X$ with $\Delta(A)\le C\Delta$.

nodes.name: Regularity boost on $J$
nodes.statement: Set $J:=G\setminus (X\cup A)$; $\delta(J)\ge (1-\varepsilon_3)v(J)$. By Lemma RegBoost, exists subhypergraph $\mathcal{D}'\subseteq {\rm Design}_{K_q^r}(J)$ with near-regular degree.

nodes.name: Nibble with reserves
nodes.statement: Build $G_1:=\mathcal{D}'$ and $G_2$ as described. Verify codegree and degree conditions, apply Theorem NibbleReserves to get $V(G_1)$-perfect matching $\mathcal{Q}_1$ which is a $K_q^r$ packing of $G$.

nodes.name: Absorb leftover via omni-absorber
nodes.statement: $L:=X\setminus Q_1$ is $K_q^r$-divisible. By definition of refined omni-absorber, $L\cup A$ admits decomposition $\mathcal{Q}_2$. Then $\mathcal{Q}_1\cup \mathcal{Q}_2$ is a $K_q^r$-decomposition of $G$.

nodes.name: Cogirth Absorber Theorem
nodes.statement: Let $q>r\ge 1$ integers. If $L$ is $K_q^r$-divisible $r$-uniform hypergraph, exists $K_q^r$-absorber $A$ of $L$ and $K_q^r$ decompositions $\mathcal{Q}_1$ of $A$, $\mathcal{Q}_2$ of $A\cup L$ such that for all $Q_1\in \mathcal{Q}_1$, $Q_2\in \mathcal{Q}_2$, $|V(Q_1)\cap V(Q_2)|\le r$.
conclusions: Exists decompositions $\mathcal{Q}_1, \mathcal{Q}_2$ with bounded pairwise intersection $\le r$

nodes.name: Min Cogirth Steiner
nodes.statement: For all $q>r\ge 1$, exist $n_0$, $\varepsilon>0$: if $G$ $K_q^r$-divisible $r$-uniform with $v(G)\ge n_0$, $\delta(G)\ge (1-\varepsilon)v(G)$, $\mathcal{Q}_1$ a $K_q^r$-packing of $G$, then exists $K_q^r$-decomposition $\mathcal{Q}_2$ with $|V(Q_1)\cap V(Q_2)|\le r$ for all $Q_1\in \mathcal{Q}_1, Q_2\in \mathcal{Q}_2$.
conclusions: Exists $K_q^r$-decomposition $\mathcal{Q}_2$ with low pairwise intersection with $\mathcal{Q}_1$

nodes.name: Better Absorber Lemma
nodes.statement: If $L$ is $K_q^r$-divisible, exists $K_q^r$-absorber $A$ for $L$ such that $A\cup L$ admits $K_q^r$-decomposition $\mathcal{Q}$ with $|V(Q)\cap V(L)|\le r$ for all $Q$, and equality only if $V(Q)\cap V(L)=V(e)$ for some $e\in L$.
conclusions: Decomposition $\mathcal{Q}$ of $A\cup L$ with bounded pairwise intersection

nodes.name: Proof of Better Absorber Lemma
nodes.statement: Construct $L'$ by adding $M(q,r)$ partial $K_q^r$'s to each edge of $L$. Apply Theorem AbsorberExistence to $L_1=L'\setminus L$ and $L_2=L'\setminus \bigcup \mathcal{Q}'$. Combine into $A=L_1\cup A_1\cup A_2$ with appropriate decompositions.

nodes.name: Cited Result Sufficiency
nodes.statement: Keevash's typicality theorem yields a weaker version of Theorem Omni with worse parameters $\Delta\sim n^{1-\varepsilon}$ and decomposition family of size $\Omega(n^{q-r})$ per edge, missing the constant-refinement property crucial for the applications.

nodes.name: Edge vs Vertex Vortex
nodes.statement: Aided by efficient omni-absorbers, this paper uses a one-step edge vortex (single random subset $E_1\subset E_0=E(K_n^r)$) instead of iterative absorption with vertex vortex.
